title: Everybody Had Advice
subtitle: Respect, not certainty, makes sense of adolescent romance
sourceCredit: Michael Maina · The Moth Radio Hour, “Live and Learn”

shot.title: A low ceiling of certainty
shot.direction: Competing advice bubbles hang low above the teen, each visually different.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: In a modest school common room, the teenager sits on a real chair under several low hovering empty advice-shapes, each a different muted contour, leaving his head and shoulders readable. His hands hold the chair edges lightly and he looks between the shapes with uncertain eyes. A second empty chair waits off to one side near a window. The symbolic shapes imply contradictory voices without any painted words, literal collision with his head or physically shrinking body.

shot.title: The first collision
shot.direction: Two bubbles bounce into each other; his body is squeezed between their directions.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: In a modest school common room, the teenager sits on a real chair under several low hovering empty advice-shapes, each a different muted contour, leaving his head and shoulders readable. shot.title: Tell them everything
shot.direction: A large bubble pushes from one side; treat the friend’s advice as an offscreen voice.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: A large warm-colored empty speech-shape presses into the composition from the left, while the teen turns toward that offscreen friend's voice. One hand lifts half-way as if about to agree, elbow attached naturally; the other still rests on the seat. His face is startled and pulled toward somebody else's confidence. Keep the school chair, window and body scale consistent, with plenty of breathing space below the symbolic ceiling. No visible friend or romantic partner is introduced.

shot.title: Pretend not to care
shot.direction: The contrary bubble pushes back from the other side.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: A differently shaped cool-purple empty advice bubble pushes from the right as the left shape remains at the edge. The teen turns back the other way, raised hand now hesitating, shoulders angled between the contradictory directions. His knees and feet remain ordinary and grounded, not twisted like a puppet. The room has not changed. The two voices are separate offscreen perspectives, not a literal fight or bullying mob.

shot.title: Smaller between answers
shot.direction: His shoulders draw in as he admits that certainty belongs to everyone else.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: The teenager draws his shoulders in and lets both hands rest loosely near his knees, eyes lowered after the competing voices. The empty advice-shapes hang above but have stopped pressing; his body stays its real adolescent size rather than magically shrinking. The spare chair and open school window remain visible. His mouth is small and honest, admitting uncertainty without tears or humiliation. Keep attention on the person under the opinions.

shot.title: A quiet chair
shot.direction: A teacher brings a chair close. The bubbles stop bouncing before they fade.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: The teacher has brought the second chair beside and slightly facing the teen, both seats clearly supported on the same floor. She sits at a respectful distance with a small open hand over her own knee; he turns toward her, no longer gripping his seat. The advice shapes have settled into faint stationary outlines high above. Their faces meet at a natural eye line, an ordinary conversation rather than a lecture or adult looming over a child.

beats.caption: Have you asked what the other person wants?
beats.speaker: TEACHER

shot.title: What does the other person want
shot.direction: The teacher asks one simple question and leaves time for an answer.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: The teacher has brought the second chair beside and slightly facing the teen, both seats clearly supported on the same floor. shot.title: A real pause
shot.direction: He looks toward the other chair instead of the floating instructions.
shot.soundDirection: Crowded overlapping chatter snapping away into the sound of two chairs.

illustration.direction: The symbolic ceiling has cleared. The teen sits more open toward the teacher, hands relaxed and one palm slightly turned upward as he recognizes the possibility of listening first. She attends quietly with a small encouraging expression, not a congratulatory sermon. Two chairs, a window and an unremarkable school room fill the warm wide panel. No crush, date, kiss, text-message reply or successful romantic outcome is shown; this is a respectful beginning, not a resolved romance.

beats.caption: No. I suppose I could listen first.
beats.speaker: TEEN
